claims.text: CoCrFeNiMn is an FCC high-entropy alloy system.
The initial CoCrFeNiMn baseline has a disordered, homogeneous FCC microstructure without substantial secondary precipitate phases.
The intervention adds a controlled but unspecified amount of Al to the alloy.
The proposed processing uses solution treatment at 1100°C followed by aging at 750°C for 20 hours.
Al addition followed by solution treatment and isothermal aging will form ordered L1₂ precipitates in the FCC matrix.
The resulting L1₂ precipitates will be coherent with the FCC matrix.
The L1₂ precipitates impede dislocation movement through precipitation hardening.
Impeded dislocation movement increases elevated-temperature yield strength.
The precipitate-strengthened microstructure enhances elevated-temperature creep resistance.
At 700–800°C, the Al-added and aged alloy will have a lower creep rate than the alloy without Al addition and subsequent aging.
At 700–800°C, the Al-added and aged alloy will have greater yield strength than the alloy without Al addition and subsequent aging.
The hypothesis is expected to apply to FCC HEAs similar to CoCrFeNiMn under controlled atmospheres at 700–800°C.
Departures from the proposed alloy composition or heat-treatment parameters may alter the outcome.
Prolonged high-temperature exposure may compromise the uniformity or stability of the L1₂ precipitates.
Insufficiently controlled processing may produce deleterious secondary phases.
